title: Forensic Telemetry Mapping and Evidence Retention Playbook
author: Arielle Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook establishes a single-source mapping for forensic telemetry across Redwood Inference services, defines retention windows and custody procedures for evidence, and documents the incident response handoff between Product/Platform, SRE, Security, and Legal. It is intended for incident responders, SREs, security engineers, and compliance reviewers who will prepare or respond to security incidents requiring forensic evidence collection and compliance reporting.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments where Redwood controls telemetry collection.
- Covers: authentication/authorization events, audit logs, model inference telemetry, kernel/runtime traces, network flows, KMS access logs, and storage access events.
- Excludes transient developer IDE logs and ephemeral debug traces that are never persisted.

Key objectives:
1) Provide deterministic mapping from incident type to the minimal telemetry set required for investigation and compliance.
2) Standardize retention, immutability, and chain-of-custody controls across regions and residency requirements.
3) Define actionable runbook steps for evidence collection, preservation, and transfer to Legal/Compliance.

Ownership and contacts:
- Primary owner: Security (Arielle Chen)
- Secondary owners: Eng-SRE (Samuel Green), Eng-Serving-Runtime (Diego Morales)
- Oncall escalation: security-oncall@redwood-inference.com

Telemetry taxonomy (canonical event types):
1) AUTHZ events: login.success, login.failure, token.issue, token.revoke, role.change, role.provisioning
2) AUTHN events: mfa.challenge, mfa.success, service-identity-auth, service-identity-fail
3) AUDIT events: api.request, api.response, api.error, admin.change, policy.update
4) RUNTIME traces: model.start_inference, model.kv_cache_hit, model.kv_cache_miss, model.quantize_path, kernel.error
5) INFRA/NW: instance.spawn, instance.terminate, ip.conn.open, ip.conn.close, nat.gateway-fail
6) STORAGE/KMS: s3.get_object, s3.put_object, kms.encrypt, kms.decrypt, kms.key_rotate

Telemetry mapping matrix (what to collect per incident class):
- Incident class: Unauthorized console access
  - Required telemetry: AUTHZ (role.change, login.*), API audit (admin.change), SSO provider logs, session tokens, console command traces, S3 access where artifacts were accessed.
- Incident class: Model exfiltration suspicion
  - Required telemetry: model.start_inference, model.kv_cache_hit/miss, api.request/response payload meta, network flows to external IPs, storage GET/PRESIGNED URLs, private deployment egress logs.
- Incident class: Privilege escalation via svc account
  - Required telemetry: service-identity-auth, role.provisioning, KMS decrypt ops, admin.change events.

Retention and residency rules (summary table):
| Data class | Default retention | Immutability | Regional residency rule | Minimum indexing tier |
|-----------|-------------------|--------------|-------------------------|----------------------|
| AUTHZ / Audit | 7 years | Write-once S3 + object lock | Region-of-origin for tenant data | hot (30d) then warm |
| Runtime traces | 90 days | Append-only in logging cluster | Global except private deployments where local only | hot (14d) |
| Network flows | 365 days (summary), 90 days (pcap) | Encrypted archival S3 | Must follow customer residency for private deployments | warm |
| KMS access logs | 7 years | Immutable audit store | Tenant-region KMS logging | cold archival |

Notes: retention values above reflect Redwood baseline for enterprise customers. Individual contracts may override values; any exception must follow the Risk & Exceptions flow (see section).

Evidence packaging and chain of custody checklist:
- When evidence is identified, create an Evidence Ticket (EVID-<INCIDENT_ID>-<YYYYMMDD>) in the incident tracker and tag with confidentiality level.
- Freeze the relevant storage paths (S3 prefixes, logging streams) using object-lock or equivalent.
- Record the following metadata for each artifact: artifact_id, collector (team-oncall), collection_time (UTC), hash (sha256), storage_path, kms_key_id, retention_policy_reference.
- Transfer artifacts to the Evidence Bucket (s3://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/) using server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and enable MFA-delete on the bucket.
- Capture a signed custody receipt: template provided below.

Custody receipt (template):
- Incident ID: <id>
- Artifact ID: <id>
- Collected by: <name + team>
- Collected at (UTC): <timestamp>
- SHA256: <hex>
- Storage location: <s3 path or archive id>
- Notes: <short justification>
- Signature (collector) and Signature (security reviewer): <name + timestamp>

Runbook: Initial evidence collection for a verified security incident
1) Triage and classify incident (Security triage) — determine incident class per taxonomy.
2) Open Evidence Ticket and assign collector: security or SRE engineer.
3) Execute containment if required (isolate affected instances, revoke tokens).
4) Snapshot all relevant boxes: live memory snapshot (if approved by Legal and if necessary), core dumps, and runtime KV caches when supported.
5) Export logs: use logging-service export CLI and include time-window +/- 2 hours around first known anomalous event. Example commands:
   - logging-cli export --service inference-api --start 2027-07-01T09:12:00Z --end 2027-07-01T11:12:00Z --output s3://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/logs/
   - audit-query "event.type:api.request AND request.path:\"/v1/generate\"" --from -2h --to +2h --out s3://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/api-requests.ndjson
6) Apply immutability: aws s3api put-object-lock-configuration --bucket redwood-evidence-<id> --object-lock-configuration ... (security to assist).
7) Compute and log artifact hashes and upload custody receipt to ticket.
8) Notify Legal/Compliance for regulatory holds before any deletion or cross-border transfer.

Special handling: private deployments and customer-managed k8s
- For private deployments where customer controls persistence, Redwood will ship a forensics collection package (collector container + manifest) executed under customer operations supervision. The package produces the same artifact metadata schema and signs outputs with Redwood-provisioned signing keys.
- For air-gapped customers, follow the Offline Evidence Transfer (OET) flow: physical media are inventoried, hashed, and transported under signed chain-of-custody.

RBAC & Evidence access controls:
- Evidence buckets and artifact indices are restricted to the evidence_readers and evidence_admins roles.
- Just-in-time access (JIT) is supported for auditors: request via access-portal with automatic short-lived credential issuance (max 8 hours). Requests are logged in AUTHZ events and require approval by Security + Legal for Confidential artifacts.
- Privileged sessions to view raw artifacts must be done through a session-proxy that records video and keystroke metadata and deposits a session-audit event.

Audit logging and query patterns for investigators:
- Canonical index fields: timestamp, event_type, service, tenant_id, user_id, ip, request_id, parent_request_id, correlation_id, sha256_artifact.
- Example investigative queries:
  - Find all admin changes for user alice@example.com in 24h window: index:audit AND event_type:admin.change AND target.user:alice@example.com AND @timestamp:[now-24h TO now]
  - Trace inference requests that produced large responses: index:api AND event_type:api.response AND body_length:>1000000 | stats count by user_id

Secure SDLC touchpoints (what dev teams must do to support forensics):
- Instrumentation: all new services must emit the canonical index fields and include request_id propagation.
- Error classification: runtime errors that may be security-relevant must map to one of the runtime trace event types.
- Testing: every release must include an observability smoke test that verifies retention and exportability of 7 sample events.
- PR requirement: changes to telemetry schema or retention policies must include an ADR and a compliance review tag.

Risk & Exceptions workflow (short):
1) Submit a Risk Exception Request (RER) in the Risk Registry with justification, compensating controls, and TTL.
2) Security + Compliance review within 5 business days.
3) If approved, implement compensating controls (e.g., additional network egress restrictions, higher-frequency snapshots) and record automatic reminders for expiry.
4) All exceptions affecting retention must be escalated to Legal for customer notification if required by contract.

SLAs and operational targets:
- Evidence readiness SLA: initial evidence snapshot (logs + primary artifacts) available within 4 hours for hosted incidents during business hours; 8 hours for off-hours.
- Artifact hash verification: 100% of collected artifacts must have a recorded checksum within 1 hour of ingestion.
- Immutability enforcement: object-lock applied within 30 minutes of artifact upload.

Compliance checklist (pre-audit):
- Confirm evidence ticket exists and custody receipts are signed.
- Validate retention policy references and regional placement for each artifact.
- Verify KMS key IDs and key rotation status (last rotation within 365 days unless justified).
- Ensure difference between raw and redacted artifacts is documented and that redactions preserve original object hashes in metadata.

Appendices:
A. Artifact metadata JSON schema (single-line example):
{"artifact_id":"EVID-12345-20270701","collector":"samuel.green","collected_at":"2027-07-01T11:02:00Z","sha256":"<hex>","storage_path":"s3://redwood-evidence/EVID-12345/...","kms_key_id":"arn:aws:kms:...","retention_policy":"audit-7y"}

B. Quick reference commands:
- Export logs: logging-cli export --service <svc> --start <ts> --end <ts> --output s3://redwood-evidence/<incident-id>/
- Lock object: aws s3api put-object-lock-configuration --bucket <bucket> --object-lock-configuration Config=...
- Compute hash: sha256sum <file>

C. Frequently asked questions:
- Q: Who approves cross-border transfer of forensic artifacts?
  A: Security + Legal must approve. If customer residency constraints exist, follow private deployment OET flow.
- Q: Can developers access raw evidence?
  A: No. Developers require a JIT approval with explicit business justification; all access is logged and time-limited.

Revision history:
- 2027-03-15: Initial draft by Arielle Chen.
- 2027-05-10: Added private deployment OET flow (reviewers: Diego Morales).
- 2027-07-02: Published with updated SLA targets and retention matrix adjustments.

End of playbook.
